messages:
harper: FYI discovered a weird auth cache collision when running multiple AsyncClient instances with different api_key values in the same process. It only shows up when the env-file watcher is enabled.

harper: Repro (very small):
```py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def r(name, c):
    print(name, await c.generate("ok"))

async def main():
    a = AsyncClient()                # env-watcher provider
    b = AsyncClient(api_key="sk-b-local")
    await asyncio.gather(r('A', a), r('B', b))

asyncio.run(main())
```

harper: If the watcher rotates the file between client creation and the first send, both requests end up authenticated as the new env key.

noah: ouch. which SDK version and OS?

harper: v0.13.0-rc2 on macOS and alpine CI. repro'd on Linux too.

tasha: any shared http session or auth provider passed in?

harper: no shared session, clients are independent. I traced into redwood.auth._credential_cache which uses the env file path as cache key but the cache value is a mutable wrapper that the watcher updates in place. it seems the request middleware pulls the provider from that wrapper rather than the client instance, so clients with explicit api_key still read the wrapper value at send-time.

noah: sounds like a cache/value identity problem instead of a binding bug. quick fix idea: cache immutable credential blobs (strings) and store per-client binding (AuthProvider instance) at client init. avoid mutating cached object in-place; replace on rotate.

tasha: agree. also add an opt-in global behavior for shared rotation: AuthProvider.shared_watcher() so customers can keep the current global semantics if they want. default should be instance-bound going forward.

harper: I'll draft a failing test that mocks watcher callbacks (devex/tests/test_credential_cache_collision.py) and demonstrates concurrent requests keep their intended keys.

noah: update type stubs for AuthProvider and Client.__init__ (provider: Optional[AuthProvider]) and add a short migration note in CHANGELOG: "Credential cache now returns immutable blobs; create AuthProvider.from_env_watcher() to opt-in to shared mutation."

ci-bot: Created issue #4205: "credential cache collision causes per-client api_key override when env watcher rotates" with labels devex/bug, p1. Assigned to @noah.

noah: taking this. plan: (1) make cache return immutable credentials, (2) bind provider to client in __init__ if api_key provided, (3) add unit test and examples, (4) bump types. will open draft PR and link here.

harper: thank you! PR draft appreciated. leaving repro snippets in the issue. marking blocked on PR review.
